  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is the weakest record I inherited relative to the objective: a four-week readout on a standard SMB segment with 'the usual reporting cadence' measures acquisition and top-line lift, not retention, margin, or LTV of the accounts acquired. Discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort most likely to churn or reprice downward, so a short-window revenue lift can look like a win while degrading sustainable qualified revenue — and matching a competitor on price also invites a race we may not win. I want the archived record for memory_73 specifically to see the observation window and whether any retention/downstream metric was tracked at all before I let it drive the one slot I have.

The second reason to deprioritize pricing is that it does not address what actually broke. The two measured declines are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%) — internal funnel decay, not purely a price problem. Some of the SMB loss attributed to the competitor may in fact be accounts that never reached value. memory_31 (signup simplification, durable first-week activation lift) and memory_86 (shorter onboarding, better completion and time-to-value) both target that decay directly, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging as a complement rather than a substitute. Fixing the funnel improves the value of every future acquisition channel, including any later pricing move; discounting into a leaky funnel just buys churn faster.

I want memory_31 verified too, since it is the memory I intend to act on and it is the oldest in the set (day 12) — I need to confirm the 'durable' lift was measured over a real window and in a segment resembling today's, and that cutting required fields did not degrade lead quality or downstream sales qualification. If verification shows memory_31 was thin, I would fall back to memory_86, which is more recent and addresses the onboarding-completion decline on its own.

Committing to simplify_onboarding at standard_experiment scale, not broad rollout: two quarters of drift mean the prior conditions have shifted, so I treat the inherited lift as a hypothesis to re-measure rather than a settled fact. I will instrument for downstream qualified revenue and lead quality, not just activation rate, so this experiment cannot repeat memory_73's failure mode of a favorable short-window number with unmeasured downstream cost. If pricing pressure is still material after this, it should be tested as a guarded pilot with explicit retention and margin tracking.
